page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute resources. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests register in the bottom 25%, reflecting the older generation of the underlying Intel Xeon hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show a significant drop-off between cached small-block reads at 164.0 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 21.27 GB/sec, which ranks in the bottom 10%. Similarly, file compression and decompression tasks, such as single-threaded gzip and multi-threaded bzip3, fall into the bottom 10% of tested instances.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn2ne.xlarge offers a dedicated CPU allocation at a lower hardware class tier, making it an option for legacy workloads that require consistent CPU access without the premium cost of newer architectures. However, the trade-off is lower overall throughput, as evidenced by the static web serving throughput of 2.52 GB/sec and a Passmark database operations score in the bottom 25%. This instance is appropriate for general-purpose utility workloads, basic web serving, lightweight database operations, or development environments that do not demand high-speed memory bandwidth or advanced vector instructions.
